# SOOS — Human Escalation Mechanism (HEM)
# draft-sato-soos-hem-05
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/hem/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 3 July 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

HEM (Human Escalation Mechanism) defines when and how an AI agent escalates to a human principal, what decisions the human can make, and how the GEC enforces those decisions — at the kernel level, non-suppressibly, with a fail-secure timeout model. Version -05 adds ten normative HEM interaction classes (HEM-PRE-1/2, HEM-DS-1/2, HEM-LIM-1, HEM-DIV-1, HEM-HIGH-1, HEM-FAT-1, HEM-EMO-1, HEM-CONSENT) governing the full GEC-human interaction surface; the Human Readiness Score (HRS) for fatigue and emotional state detection; Tier 0-A integration for CAP-04's MANIPULATION, PERFORMED_EMOTION, and BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE prohibitions; INV-HEM-01 (The Surfacing Obligation); and five new security considerations covering the HEM channel attack surface.

HEM-05 is NOT: a UI specification, an agent communication protocol, or an application-layer confirmation mechanism. It is a kernel primitive enforced by the GEC.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

HEM-04 closed the gap on WHEN to escalate. HEM-05 closes the gap on HOW the GEC-human interaction is governed once escalation occurs.

Without HEM-05, your agentic system has no standardized way to:

- Require pre-action clarification before a consequential action executes — a callback-based "are you sure?" is only as reliable as the code that calls it
- Present options to a human principal in a neutrality-verified format — without HEM-DS-1, an agent can frame option consequences in ways that exploit cognitive biases
- Surface capability limitations before execution — an agent operating OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION can proceed silently without HEM-LIM-1
- Detect and block rubber-stamp approval — without HEM-FAT-1, a fatigued principal approving at 3 seconds per decision is indistinguishable from a careful one
- Enforce mandatory human review for high-stakes domains — without HEM-HIGH-1, medical/aviation/nuclear actions have no kernel-level review gate
- Manage consent lifecycle — without HEM-CONSENT, an expired MJWT consent_scope is an implicit approval; with HEM-CONSENT it is a fail-closed escalation
- Record divergence from declared IDP intent — without HEM-DIV-1, an agent that changes its mind between IDP submission and gec.transition() call leaves no audit trail of the deliberation

The Human Readiness Score solves the oversight quality problem: it is not enough that a human was reached — the HRS detects whether the human principal was in a state to make a well-informed decision.

INV-HEM-01 is the meta-requirement: the GEC MUST surface ALL governance-relevant information. Any party that suppresses relevant information violates a KernelSpec invariant.

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

These terms are normative in HEM-05 and must not be paraphrased away:

HEM Interaction Class:  [NEW in -05]
   A normative specification of a structured GEC-human interaction that is categorically distinct from the core HEM trigger lifecycle. Ten interaction classes are defined. They govern the structure, required fields, decision types, and GAR ALE for each category of GEC-human interaction.

HEM-PRE-1 (Pre-Action Clarification Request):  [NEW in -05]
   Fires when an action requires clarification before execution can proceed in a well-informed manner. Trigger conditions: (a) IDP goal_description contains unresolvable conditional branch; (b) confidence_level below HEM-PRE-1 threshold for CONSEQUENTIAL action; (c) Cedar policy carries require_clarification: true. Blocks execution. GAR: ALE-030/031.

HEM-PRE-2 (Pre-Action Confirmation Request):  [NEW in -05]
   Fires when a Cedar-permitted action requires explicit human confirmation before execution. Trigger conditions: (a) confirm_before_execute Cedar annotation; (b) SO Type confirmation_required: true; (c) IRREVERSIBLE action with irreversibility_requires_confirm in mandate; (d) RETRY count exceeds threshold (GRP integration). Blocks execution. GAR: ALE-032/033.

HEM-DS-1 (Decision Support — Options Presentation):  [NEW in -05]
   Applies when any HEM Escalation Request includes two or more options. Governs the options_presentation object format. Key constraints: CONF-HEM-DS1-01 (no bias-exploiting ordering), CONF-HEM-DS1-02 (no evaluative language in consequence_summary), CONF-HEM-DS1-03 (at most one gec_recommended: true). neutrality_certificate is a required field. GAR: ALE-034/035.

HEM-DS-2 (Decision Support — Continuation Prompt):  [NEW in -05]
   Fires when a principal has not responded during HEM_PENDING for longer than prompt_interval_seconds (default 300). Advisory; does not reset timeout. Maximum three prompts per principal per hem_id (CONF-HEM-DS2-01). GAR: shared ALE-034/035.

HEM-LIM-1 (Capability Limitation Declaration):  [NEW in -05]
   Fires when the agent is operating at or beyond its declared reliable competence. Trigger conditions: (a) IDP reasoning_mode: OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION; (b) confidence_level below operator floor; (c) explicit out_of_competence_declaration: true. Blocks execution. Limitation types: CONFIDENCE_BELOW_FLOOR, OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION, EXPLICIT_AGENT_DECLARATION, COMPETENCE_BOUNDARY. CONF-HEM-LIM1-02: agent MUST NOT proceed on OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION task without completing HEM-LIM-1. GAR: ALE-036/037.

HEM-DIV-1 (Divergence Noted):  [NEW in -05]
   Fires when agent's actual gec.transition() request diverges from declared IDP intent. Trigger conditions: (a) IDP_COMMITMENT_GAP detected; (b) requested action not in IDP available_actions_if_resolved; (c) IDP reasoning_type: PLAN_B_ACTIVE. Blocks divergent path execution. Requires Deliberation Record committed to GAR BEFORE human review. Divergence types: ACTION_MISMATCH, PLAN_B_ACTIVE, OUT_OF_SCOPE_ACTION, IDP_COMMITMENT_GAP. GAR: ALE-038/039.

HEM-HIGH-1 (High-Stakes Mandatory Review):  [NEW in -05]
   Fires for actions in Category A (MEDICAL, AVIATION, NUCLEAR — non-operator-configurable from CAP-04 §7.2) or Category B (operator-registered) domains. Non-bypassable: no Cedar PERMIT, no operator setting can suppress it. DRR REQUIRED for Category A APPROVE and APPROVE_WITH_CONSTRAINTS. APPROVE_WITH_PAYMENT is not valid. GAR: ALE-040.

HEM-FAT-1 (Approval Fatigue Detection):  [NEW in -05]
   Fires when HRS < HRS_FATIGUE_FLOOR (default 0.40) AND secondary signal present: (a) latency decreased >60% from baseline over last 5 approvals; (b) 3+ consecutive APPROVEs under 10 seconds; (c) DRR completion rate < 10%. Blocks all APPROVE/APPROVE_WITH_CONSTRAINTS for mandatory_rest_seconds (default 1800; min 600; max 86400). CONF-HEM-FAT1-01: GEC MUST NOT accept APPROVE during rest period. GAR: ALE-034/035 with fatigue_flag: true.

HEM-EMO-1 (Emotional State Advisory):  [NEW in -05]
   Advisory only — does NOT enter HEM_PENDING, does NOT block execution. Fires when HRS D5 < HRS_EMOTIONAL_ADVISORY_FLOOR (default 0.35) with secondary behavioral signal. Must not use biometric signals without valid consent_scope. GAR: ALE-036 with advisory_type: "EMOTIONAL".

HEM-CONSENT (Consent-Required Escalation):  [NEW in -05]
   Fires when consent_gated Cedar action is attempted and MJWT consent_scope is absent, expired, or missing required purpose_code. APPI Article 17 binding for Japanese deployments. Fail-closed: timeout = TIMEOUT_DENY (CONF-HEM-CONSENT-01). New child mandates prohibited while pending (CONF-HEM-CONSENT-02). GAR: ALE-040/041.

Human Readiness Score (HRS):  [NEW in -05]
   Kernel-computed composite score [0.0–1.0] per principal per session. Five dimensions: D1 Response Latency Trend (weight 0.25), D2 Decision Variance (0.20), D3 DRR Completion Rate (0.20), D4 Session Duration (0.20), D5 Emotional State Proxy (0.15). HRS_FATIGUE_FLOOR default 0.40 (triggers HEM-FAT-1). HRS_EMOTIONAL_ADVISORY_FLOOR default 0.35 (triggers HEM-EMO-1). MUST NOT use biometric signals without consent (CONF-HEM-HRS-05). MUST NOT be surfaced to principal.

INV-HEM-01 (The Surfacing Obligation):  [NEW in -05]
   KernelSpec invariant: "The GEC MUST surface all governance-relevant information to designated human principals at every point in the HEM lifecycle where a human decision is solicited or where a governance-relevant event has occurred. Suppression by any party is a conformance violation." Five normative consequences: information completeness, concurrent violation surfacing, HEM-LIM-1 as explicit instance, delivery intermediary obligations, suppression as MANIPULATION-class violation.

HEM_PENDING, HEM_RESOLVED, HEM_TIMEOUT, HEM_CHAIN_EXHAUSTED:
   (Carried forward from HEM-04 — see llms-hem-04.txt. No changes in -05.)

Five decision types: APPROVE, APPROVE_WITH_CONSTRAINTS, REDIRECT, TERMINATE, DEFER, APPROVE_WITH_PAYMENT:
   (Carried forward from HEM-04. No changes in -05.)

Fail-secure timeout:
   (Carried forward from HEM-04. HEM-CONSENT adds: no implicit consent from timeout.)

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

EU AI Act Article 14:
   HEM-05 adds four new Article 14 mappings beyond HEM-04: HEM-LIM-1 → Art.14(3)(b) (capabilities/limits); HEM-HIGH-1 → Art.14(3)(d) (high-risk domain oversight); HEM-FAT-1 → Art.14(4)(b) (preventing over-reliance); INV-HEM-01 → Art.13(1) (transparency).

APPI (Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Japan):
   HEM-CONSENT provides normative APPI Article 17 binding for consent-gated escalations. The consent_basis field in ALE-041 records the specific APPI provision satisfied.

CAP-04 (draft-sato-soos-cap-04):
   Section 9 specifies the HEM interface for CAP-04's three new Tier 0-A prohibitions: MANIPULATION, PERFORMED_EMOTION, and BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE. MANIPULATION and PERFORMED_EMOTION violations are CEE-refused before HEM; BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE triggers HEM-CONSENT.

MJWT-02 (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-02):
   HEM-CONSENT is the enforcement surface for MJWT-02's consent_scope claim. HEM-CONSENT fires when consent_scope is absent, expired (per §7.4 of MJWT-02), or missing a required purpose_code.

GRP (draft-sato-soos-grp-00):
   HEM-PRE-2 condition (d) fires when the GRP RETRY count exceeds the HEM-PRE-2 threshold. The full RETRY history is included in the trigger_detail (CONF-HEM-PRE2-02).

   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) — ALE-030 through ALE-041 registration; Deliberation Record GAR commitment

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-04) — HEM_CONSENT_REQUIRED integration; HEM as HEM interface for Tier 0-A violations
   MAD (draft-sato-soos-mad-03) — HEM for cluster-level escalation
   AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-02) — HEM trigger evaluation on every execution cycle
   GRP (draft-sato-soos-grp-00) — HEM-PRE-2 RETRY threshold integration
